Your first problem is AMD - as much as I love AMD as a company, their linux video drivers seem to have been coded by autistic llamas.

Your second - the black screen from cold boot - is likely a combination of AMD and you hard reset (holding down the power button to kill the PC and start over), which isn't your fault, sometimes there is just an issue like that where you have no choice. I've noticed that some distros have problem with sleep and hibernation. Quite often I'd wake my PC and the lock screen wouldn't accept any input - I couldn't type my password or anything, and would have to restart X to log in.

My suggestion: check your HDD. It COULD be the issue (though I'm inclined to believe it is not). I used Mint for nearly a year after using Ubuntu for over 4 years. As someone else here told me: there are some extremely good distros that don't get the coverage that "main stream" distros do - yet are more reliable, stable, compatible, etc.

I would suggest giving another distro a shot - Manjaro has my vote - but there's no "wrong" answer. Also, though your stress testing turned out well, I'm telling you right now that is NOT an indication of stability when you are using AMD drivers, unfortunately. They are horrible. It seems that AMD is starting to take this issue seriously, but they are shit for the time being. Also, are you using proprietary or legacy drivers? I'm not terribly up-to-date on AMD driver families so IDK how old your card is but there is a rather specific demarcation line between legacy hardware and stuff that's compatible with the proprietary driver.

All in all, I would highly suggest giving another distro a shot. I'm no member of the Fanatical Brotherhood of the Perpetual Arch Proselytizers, but seriously - as someone who had there share of inconsistent little issues on mint 17, 17.1, 17.2, and 17.3, Manjaro has been a god damned miracle. But to repeat myself: there's no actual right or wrong distro - there's the one that works for you, and all the others :)
